title: Convergent review triage & rollforward checklist (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic scratchpad for triaging incoming PRs and making fast rollforward vs revert decisions. Not a final playbook — this is my personal checklist and a place to capture heuristics we can later formalize.

Context / goals:
- Keep main green and fast; avoid large reverts unless rollout-safe.
- Empower reviewers to surface risk signals (latency, cache, backward compatibility, infra changes) in one quick pass.
- Provide a minimal set of actions so on-call / triage lead can make stopgap decisions (block/hold/merge+monitor/rollback).

Quick triage rubric (30–90s):
1) PR size & surface area
   - tiny (< 200 LOC, localized): low risk unless touches serialization, migrations, or public API.
   - medium (200–1000 LOC or touching multiple packages): moderate risk — require smoke tests and a clear rollback plan.
   - large (>1000 LOC or infra changes): high risk — prefer canary + feature-flag or staged rollforward.
2) Runtime/infra impact
   - GPU/serving/runtime changes, batcher, KV cache, quantization: assume high risk.
   - UI, docs, small config: low risk.
3) Data/compatibility hazards
   - schema migrations, tokenization, saved inference artifacts: require migration plan and one-upgrade test.
   - model version pinning changes: check fallback paths.
4) Test coverage / CI signals
   - CI green + integration smoke passes: +1 toward merge.
   - Flaky tests or long-running CI failures: block until fixed or escalate for canary-only.

Minimal review checklist (what I run through during a pass):
- Is the intent stated clearly in the PR description? If not: ask for one-sentence summary.
- Does the PR include an expected user-facing change or migration step? If yes: add to changelog/upgrade notes.
- Are there new runtime dependencies (native libs, system packages)? If yes: check infra acceptance and packaging.
- Does the change touch hotpath (infer loop, batching, cache eviction)? If yes: request microbench + latency regression check.
- Any silent behavioral changes (different tokenization, rounding, random seeds)? If yes: flag for evals team.
- Security/permissions: ensure privilege-scope is minimal.
- Observability: are there sufficient logs/metrics/traces to detect regressions? If not: ask for at least one metric and a log line.
- Rollback plan: is there a clear revert or feature-flag toggle? If no: ask for it for medium/high-risk PRs.

Decision outcomes (quick options):
- Merge+Monitor: for low/medium risk with good tests + metrics; schedule follow-up smoke check in SLO/metrics dashboard.
- Hold (block until): flaky CI, missing rollback, unresolved infra dependency.
- Canary-only: merge with small percentage or internal team, observe for 24–48h.
- Revert immediately: catastrophic user-facing regression or data-loss bug.

Rollforward vs revert decision tree (notes to self):
- If failure is detectable quickly via metric and revert is simple -> prefer revert.
- If revert is costly (DB migration) but we have a safe forward-fix available -> prefer rollforward with strict canary and tight alerting.
- If uncertain: create a short incident runbook before taking action and assign a single owner to execute.

Refactor follow-ups (capture things to do after merge):
- Add unit tests to cover the specific edge case we patched in PR.
- Extract a small helper (3-4 LOC) that makes intent clearer and simplifies future reviews.
- Add an entry in the "review heuristics" doc about this pattern.

Practical reviewer heuristics (shortcuts):
- Read the first 5 and last 5 changed files to get the scope.
- Grep for TODO/TBD/XXX in changed files — often indicates unfinished work.
- If a change touches 3+ services, ping owners in PR body before merging.
- Prefer short, action-oriented review comments; one-liners to approve or block.

Common anti-patterns to call out quickly:
- Changing default behavior without config toggle.
- Burying schema changes in helper code with no migration note.
- Relying on flaky tests as proof-of-correctness.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (for follow-ups or playbook):
- How to standardize a "fast canary" flow for Dedicated customers? (capture steps and sample CLI commands)
- Can we add an automated diff that highlights hotpath latency-sensitive lines? (ask SRE/infra)
- Where to store a minimal rollback checklist template so on-call can run it from Slack?

Quick commands + snippets to paste in PRs / Slack when triaging:
- "Tagging oncall: please run canary-rolling for PR#8421 and monitor token-latency metric for 30m."
- Revert template: `git revert -m 1 <merge-commit>` + `ci/integration-smoke --short`

Notes to self (voice-of-author):
- Keep the playbook tiny — people will not read a wall of text during outages.
- Collect 3 real incident examples where rollforward vs revert decision mattered and add short case notes.

Recent example: GH PR #8421 (linked above) — medium-sized change to batcher prioritization. CI green but integration showed 3% latency uplift in one region. We can: 1) revert (fast), or 2) canary+patch (slower). Decided: canary-only for 24h with metrics dashboard prewired. Outcome: revert later when patch introduced a memory leak. Capture as postmortem note.

End of scratchpad — move select items to shared playbook after 2-3 iterations.
